verdicts.why: Names a route along which something moves; no attitude toward it.
An established track or way; purely descriptive, as in 'the path just admitted three'.
States that someone meets the standards for a task; the fitness is the meaning, not an added approval.
'Limited, not absolute' describes the scope of a statement or support without judging it.
Officially credentialed; a matter of record, not of attitude.
'Contingent on something else' is a plain logical description.
A grammatical term for a modified noun; no judgement possible.
A short account of an incident; the word names the form, and the sentences treat it as a neutral thing to relate with humour or store in memory.
Plain name of a profession; the snobbery in 'a country attorney' belongs to the speaker's view of the referent, not to the word.
Names a reddening of the face; the cause may be shame or surprise, but the word itself reports without judging.
A rosy healthy colour; the pleasantness is the meaning, not an attitude beyond it.
Names a cosmetic product; descriptive.
'Typical or distinctive' says a thing is representative of its source without saying that is good or bad.
'Annoyed and irritable' is a mood report; the word's domestic, understated flavour is register and degree rather than contempt or affection for the person.
Lying crosswise, as in 'cross walk'; a spatial description.
Well known or recognizable, as of a carriage or livery; no attitude toward the thing.
'Familiar with' a saying means knowing it; descriptive of knowledge only.
'Common and ordinary, not strange' describes without judging; the presumptuous 'familiar way' of calling is a different sense not glossed here.
'To this place'; archaic register, but no attitude toward anything.
Free from bias is a state that can be asserted or denied ('impossible for me to be impartial'); its desirability is the referent's, and the word adds no approval beyond the meaning.
Showing no favouritism; a plain description of conduct, the same as 'unbiased' or 'even-handed'.
'Inclined to think' reports a leaning of opinion; no judgement of anyone.
Feeling willing or disposed toward something; descriptive of the subject's own disposition.
To make someone receptive; a neutral causative with no attitude built in.
To bend the head as in a bow; a physical motion.
'Be at an angle'; geometric description only.
Turning the ear to listen; a physical action with no evaluation.
A wrong unjustly done is a bad referent named in a formal, plain word; the injustice is the meaning, and the word adds no further sneer or sympathy.
Physical damage to the body; an unpleasant referent named plainly.
An accident causing hurt; the word takes no side.
